- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 5–10% for the immediate next period.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% over 3–5 days), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, consider mean reversion in 10–15 day horizon.
- If model consistently underestimates in low-sentiment periods, consider adding a 2–3% upward bias to forecast for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >5% avg. daily gain), model often lags — adjust forecast to reflect momentum, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overreact — reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is mixed or low, model tends to underestimate — apply a 2–4% upward adjustment to forecast for 5–10 day horizon.
